title: What Field Service Software Actually Saves You
meta: Cut the hype. Here's the real math on field service software — fewer missed calls, faster quotes, automatic follow-up — using numbers from your own shop.
short: Skip the hype. Here's the real time-and-money math on field service software, run with your own numbers.
statLabel: Two hours of admin a week handed back = roughly 100 hours a year

body.answer: The real payback from software is measured in recovered hours and captured leads — run it with your own numbers, not a vendor's.
body.html:
Every software company promises to "save you time and grow your business." Cool. How much, exactly? Nobody says, because the honest answer depends on your shop. So instead of hype, let's build the math with numbers only you can fill in. Plug in your real figures as we go. If the total's small, don't buy. If it's big, you have your answer.

Three places software actually moves money: the calls you miss, the quotes you're slow on, and the follow-ups that never happen. Let's price each one.

body.h2: Leak one: the calls you don't answer
body.answer: Every missed call that books with a competitor instead is a full job's revenue gone, and software that texts back plugs that leak.
body.html:
You're on a roof. The phone rings. You miss it. That caller doesn't leave a voicemail, they call the next guy. How many of those happen in a week? Two? Put your average job value on it. Two missed callers a week who each would've been, say, a few hundred dollars, is real money walking to a competitor every single week.

Speed is the whole game here: responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd). A missed-call-text-back feature answers instantly even when your hands are full. We break down exactly how that works in missed-call text-back for contractors.

body.h2: Leak two: slow quotes and dead follow-up
body.answer: Quotes that take days to send and never get chased are the single biggest silent revenue leak software fixes automatically.
body.html:
How long between a site visit and the quote landing in the customer's inbox? If it's days, you're losing jobs to whoever quoted same-day. Software that lets you build and send a quote from the driveway closes that gap. Now the follow-up: of the quotes you do send, how many go unchased? Each un-chased quote is a job you did the work to earn and then let drift.

Software chases automatically. It nudges the customer, reminds you, and keeps the quote alive while you're on the next job. Even recovering one extra won job a month changes the whole math. Run your number: your average job value, times one or two more wins a month, times twelve.

Do that multiplication with a real figure and it gets loud fast. Say your average job is a few hundred dollars and software helps you win just one extra a month. That's that number twelve times over the year, from quotes you were already sending and just letting go cold. For most shops that single line, one more won job a month, already clears the entire annual cost of the tool before you count a single hour saved.

body.answer: Stack the recovered hours against the monthly cost; if saved time plus captured jobs beats the fee, it's a buy.
body.html:
Now total it. Say software hands back two hours a week of admin, that's roughly 100 hours a year you're not doing paperwork at 9pm. Add the missed calls you'd now catch and the quotes you'd now win. Stack all of that against the monthly fee (check current pricing in the reviews hub, it changes). If saved time plus captured jobs clears the cost by a wide margin, buy. If it's close, wait.

That's the honest test. Not vibes, not fear of looking behind, just your numbers. Want someone to run them with you? Talk to a human who'll tell you if the math doesn't work.

faq.q: How much time does field service software actually save?
faq.a: It depends on your admin load, but a shop that hands back two hours a week of paperwork gets roughly 100 hours a year back. Run your own number — the honest answer is yours to calculate, not ours to guess.

faq.q: Does the missed-call feature really matter?
faq.a: Yes. Responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd). An instant text-back catches callers who'd otherwise dial a competitor.

faq.q: How do I know if it's worth the monthly cost?
faq.a: Add up saved hours plus the extra jobs you'd capture from faster response and chased quotes. If that clears the monthly fee by a wide margin, buy. If it's close, you're not ready yet.
